mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate below 0.5% signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 0.5% occurs in more than 60% of 20-day forward return periods, but average return is negative (mean < 0) or t-test for positive returns against null of zero returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate above 4.5% signals restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% occurs in more than 60% of 20-day forward return periods, but average return is positive (mean > 0) or t-test for negative returns against null of zero returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous federal funds rate below 0.5% and unemployment rate above 5.0% signals a 'soft landing' scenario where the Fed cuts rates to support the economy without inflation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Condition (FEDFUNDS < 0.5% AND UNRATE > 5.0%) occurs in more than 60% of 20-day forward return periods, but average return is negative (mean < 0) or t-test for positive returns against null of zero returns is not significant (p > 0.05).
